notes: The perp ladder keeps the NEAR staked and sells 10% of the stake short at the close after each 10% rise, at most 50%, buying each slice back after a 10% fall.

The short that never trades sells 25% of the stake at the start and buys it back at the end, with the same dollars on the venue; it collected +4.99 pp a year in funding on Hyperliquid against the ladder's +7.84 pp, so most of the funding is paid to any short.

Funding is set by each venue's formula. Between 2025-11-12 and 2026-10-30, Hyperliquid paid shorts 10.92% a year and Binance 3.91%; Hyperliquid's formula adds a fixed interest term, and its rate sat exactly at that term in 77.6% of hours, the hours the perpetual traded close to the spot price. Shorts paid in 7.5% of Hyperliquid's hours, 26.3% of Binance's settlements and 55.6% of Kraken's hours.

Against holding, the ladder averaged +16.88 pp on Hyperliquid and -16.23 pp on Binance, with a worst window of -200.85 pp; the claim that patient holders capture NEAR's volatility tests that against shuffled histories.

Staked NEAR cannot be posted on the venue, so dollars worth the most the ladder can be short sit there; after rises they are topped up, because that value grows and to cover losses on the short, with transfers taking 3 days. At the worst, the dollars sent less those brought home reached 476% of the stake's starting value on Hyperliquid and 746% on Binance. 0 windows on Hyperliquid and 0 on Binance were liquidated at a 5% maintenance margin on both venues, half the initial margin at Hyperliquid's 10× maximum leverage; the closest call left equity at 2.72× the maintenance level on Hyperliquid and 2.07× on Binance. The table shows thinner collateral and slower transfers.

A redraw picks blocks of 30 days with replacement, so it can leave out the richest months; each day keeps its price move, its high and its funding together. Redrawing breaks NEAR's longer swings, which by itself moves the average to -17.82 pp on Hyperliquid, so the redraws are centred on the real result and show only how far it moves with the months drawn.
Hyperliquid's NEAR perpetual held about $137 million of open positions at the snapshot. near.com says it routes perpetual trades to Hyperliquid; its own market list and fees are not in this data.
Fees use Hyperliquid's published base taker rate, 0.045%, on both venues, and every trade fills 0.10% against the holder; the table shows wider fills and a fill one close later.

Hyperliquid's terms are reported to count US persons among its Restricted Persons, and Binance's futures to exclude them; neither was read first-hand here. Kraken's instrument record lists only non-US platforms for its NEAR perpetual.

Coinbase Derivatives has listed a US-regulated NEAR perpetual-style future since 2026-02-28, 500 NEAR a contract and margined in dollars, which US customers trade through Coinbase Financial Markets; it held about $7.54 million of open positions at the snapshot. Coinbase's help pages, read 2026-11-13, say access needs an approved application and an eligible address and may not be available in every jurisdiction; they name no US state as excluded. An approved US holder can run the ladder there, but its 259 days of daily bars fall short of a one-year window, so neither claim reads it.

Coinbase's margin for a NEAR short is 56.2% of its value overnight and 20.0% intraday. The ladder keeps dollars worth 1.00× the most it can be short on the venue, which covers both; with no top-up, though, a short backed by dollars equal to its value meets the overnight margin after a rise of about 28%.
